S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

symptom.disease_info: Adjustment Disorder is characterized by emotional or behavioral symptoms that develop in response to an identifiable psychosocial stressor and become clinically significant through disproportionate distress or functional impairment. The course is time-limited relative to the stressor and is distinguished from primary mood, anxiety, trauma-related, or behavioral disorders by the clear stressor-linked onset and the absence of a more specific syndrome explaining the presentation.

patient.stressor_event: Gaining a new family member (e.g., birth, adoption, older adult moving in)
patient.stressor: Thomas and his wife took in her widowed father after a fall made living alone impractical, turning Thomas’s quiet workshop routines and carefully budgeted handyman plans into a daily schedule of caregiving, home modifications, and shared household decisions. At first he tried to treat the change like another practical project, building grab bars from reclaimed materials and reorganizing rooms, but over the next 5 months his emotional and behavioral reactions to the new family arrangement began interfering with licensing paperwork, small repair jobs, and his usual community commitments. The strain became clinically significant when his marriage, workshop productivity, and basic follow-through all suffered despite the stressor itself being understandable and ongoing. After missing an important contractor-license filing date and recognizing that fishing trips were no longer restoring him, he accepted a referral from his primary care clinic to outpatient psychiatric care.

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.
S081.manifestation: I’m here because ever since my father-in-law moved in, I’ve been snapping at my wife over little house things, putting off jobs and paperwork I used to stay on top of, and I just can’t seem to get my head quiet even when I’m out in the workshop or trying to fish.

add_requirements.Symptoms must develop within 3 months of: My father-in-law moved in after his fall, and within the first couple of months I noticed I was already falling behind on paperwork and arguing with my wife over household changes.
add_requirements.Within 6 months of the termination of th: The situation hasn’t really ended—he’s still living with us and the caregiving changes are still part of daily life—so I haven’t had a stretch where things were back to normal afterward.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I missed an important contractor-license filing date and have had to turn down or delay small repair jobs because I’m not keeping up the way I used to. At home, the strain has put real tension into my marriage and made it harder to follow through on family responsibilities.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about five months, since shortly after my father-in-law moved into our house.
